title: UML class diagrams
idea: A UML class diagram draws each class as a box of fields and methods, and each relationship as a line whose style names the link.
points: A box has three parts: name, fields, then methods; `-` is private, `+` public.
A hollow triangle means is-a: `extends`, or a dashed line for `implements`.
A filled diamond is composition: parts live and die with their whole.
A plain arrow is association; a dashed arrow is a dependency, like a parameter.

hero.title: The order model (symbols in Mermaid tab)

edges.label: owns 0..*
edges.caption: Composition: real UML puts a filled diamond at the `Order` end. Its lines live and die with it.

edges.label: placed by
edges.caption: Association, plain arrow: `Order` keeps a field that points to a `Customer` that lives on its own.

edges.label: uses
edges.caption: Dependency, dashed arrow: `Payment` is only a parameter of `pay`, never stored.

edges.label: implements
edges.caption: Realization, dashed line with hollow triangle: `CardPayment` implements the `Payment` interface.

code.title: Diagram as Mermaid text
code.caption: Mermaid draws this text as a class diagram. Each arrow style is one relationship kind.

walk.text: One class box: fields with `-`, methods with `+` and a return type.
`<<interface>>` marks a contract rather than a class.
`*--` is composition and `-->` is association; quoted numbers are multiplicity.
`..>` is a dependency; `<|..` is realization of an interface.

code.title: The same model in Java
code.caption: Every line in the diagram maps to a field, a parameter or an `implements`.

walk.text: Realization: the class implements the interface.
Composition: the list is private and only `Order` adds to it.
Association: a `Customer` made elsewhere is passed in and kept.
`Order` builds each `OrderLine` and never shares it, so the diamond is filled.
Dependency: `Payment` is used during the call, then forgotten.

pitfalls: Do not draw every getter; show the fields and methods that explain the design.
Use a hollow diamond (aggregation) when a part can outlive its whole.
Add multiplicity like `1..*` on links; interviewers ask about it.

quiz.q: `Order.pay(Payment payment)` uses `Payment` but never stores it. Which UML line fits?
options: A solid line with a hollow triangle
quiz.why: A type used only as a parameter or local variable is a dependency. Association needs a field that keeps the reference.

takeaway: Boxes show classes; the line style tells is-a, owns, knows or uses.
